topic: Effects of Temperature on Food and Medicines
key_concepts: Food spoilage is caused by growth of molds and bacteria
Changing temperature helps prevent food spoilage
Pasteurization heats food at 60°C to 66°C for 30-40 minutes then cools it immediately
Refrigeration keeps food at low temperature so microorganisms become less active
Drying removes moisture needed by microorganisms to grow
Canning heats food and seals it in an airtight container
Fermentation is a chemical reaction induced by yeasts, bacteria, enzymes, or molds
Ultrahigh temperature processing heats products and seals them under germ-free conditions
Heat, air, light, and moisture can damage medicine
Medicines should be stored in a cool, dry place away from heat and out of children's reach
Reading labels and checking expiration dates help use medicines safely
